title: (performance) A draw whose pipeline is not made yet compiles it on the render thread; only Vulkan with graphics pipeline libraries gets a quick link.
note: Design (read 11-18, E5's first item, with P-052 and N-1067): a stage's pipelines are made while it loads, and a draw never compiles. (1) Pipelines are registered as the stage's materials register (registries_, game thread, during the load); the render thread queues the new ones each frame (render_core.cpp, pipelines_queued_) for low-priority workers. The game's load already ends at one gate, GameSystemSceneController::isReadyToStartScene (the load screen's nerve waits there for the scene's worker): it also asks the host that every pipeline registered so far is made (Pipelines::pending() for the set queued, the workers raised to normal priority while the game waits). The load screen keeps stepping as it does for the scene's own load. (2) A draw whose pipeline is still missing in play (a material registered after the load, a settings change) is skipped for that frame and its job moved to the front of the queue at normal priority, never built on the render thread; Vulkan with pipeline libraries keeps its quick link. A miss is a timeline event and counted (made by draws first stays 0 after a stage's first picture). Proof: a tour on a cold cache (the cache files removed) on D3D12, Vulkan and the tablet: no create_now build on the render thread after a stage's first picture, frame times at first entry to three galaxies against today's, pictures the same, step-hash replays the same. 11-23 R1.2: the gate is NEBULA_OPTION_SCENE_PIPELINES in exeInitializeScene (isReadyToStartScene reads the nerve it sets); with fixed steps the game never waits, the render thread drains the queue before its next picture; 38 forms the game registered only at their first draw were added to site_pipelines.txt; stops no tour played: P-371.

title: (wrong behaviour, suspected) Android's restart starts the new activity in the `:game` process and kills that same process in the same UI-thread task.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed. GameActivity.restartGame (on the UI thread) calls startActivity(GameActivity, NEW_TASK|CLEAR_TASK) and then Process.killProcess(myPid) at once; startActivity only asks the system, which starts the new GameActivity in the process named :game, and that is the one being killed: whether the new one lands in the dying process or a fresh one depends on timing (P-099's CLEAR_TASK also drops the launcher). Design (the ProcessPhoenix pattern): the game asks the launcher's process (a small exported-false activity or service there, Intent with the restart kind) and ends its own process; the launcher's side waits for the old :game pid to be gone (ActivityManager.getRunningAppProcesses, or the pid file) and then starts GameActivity in the task it belongs to, without CLEAR_TASK (P-099). Proof: a tablet run through the harness that asks for the restart 20 times and reads 20 new pids, each start check passing.

note: Design (read 11-18, E6b with I-002 and P-156): an in-between picture differs from its list's step picture only in the blended rows (transforms, the camera's view) and in which items a moved bound culls. So each draw pass is recorded once per list, at its first picture (DrawRecorder ops, draw_record.h), with every row read through the rows base (encoder set_rows, walk_.rows_address) as the one patched value; an in-between picture writes its blended rows into a new rows slice and replays the recorded ops with that base: no walk of the items, no material or pipeline lookups. Culling: an item culled at both ends of the pair stays culled (the bound's union over the pair, a test at record time), so a replay never misses one; items culled at one end only are recorded and drawn. Passes whose inputs do not depend on t (2D layers not marked present-time, the frame copy of a step picture) are replayed as recorded. The GPU work stays a full frame (a new picture of moved objects); its cost is P-156's, measured per pass. title: (hang at start, macOS) the game thread slept for hours in its first frame wait on a Mac that had slept since its start: the wait's due moment was a std::chrono::steady_clock value read as a qpc_now() moment, and on Apple the two are different clocks; no picture was ever shown, the window stayed transparent, the log said nothing
note: Found 11-23 from the owner's sample (the game thread's every sample in one nanosleep under svc_frame_wait / PreciseWait::until) and LLVM 22.1.6 libcxx/src/chrono.cpp: steady_clock on Apple reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, which counts the time the Mac sleeps; qpc_now() on Apple is CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW, which does not. Windows (QueryPerformanceCounter on both sides) and Linux and Android (CLOCK_MONOTONIC on both) are the same clock, so it never showed there, nor on GitHub's freshly started Macs. Mended at the root: host_main.cpp svc_frame_wait keeps its due moments on the runtime's clock in nanoseconds (galaxy::FrameDue, frame_due.h); qpc_of is gone (qpc_from_ns takes the runtime clock's own nanoseconds); a moment more than max(8 periods, 250 ms) ahead is one log line and a wait of one period. tools/check_clock_domains.py (gate test) refuses qpc_of and a line that names steady_clock with the runtime's clock. Audit of the whole tree (read): no other place turns one clock into the other; steady_clock lengths that span a Mac's sleep count the sleep (benchmark stall timeouts, luma_net timeouts, a mod's time.monotonic_ns): a design effect, not mended; host_main.cpp next_frame_start now takes the runtime clock's nanoseconds and compares them with render_core's g_last_present_ns, which is steady_clock-based: the same clock on Windows, the only system that compiles it; comments that say CLOCK_MONOTONIC for qpc_now on Apple remain in sdl_host.h, host_window.h and present_slots.h (Apple's qpc_now is CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW). Not shown: a Mac of ours that has slept (the fault can only show on one).

title: (missing feature, Linux, after the beta) DLSS is not in the Linux version
note: Found 11-23 (the owner asked why DLSS is not offered on Linux). Read 11-23: NVIDIA's Streamline (github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline, README and docs/ProgrammingGuide.md line 15: "Windows PC with Windows 10 RS3 (64-bit) or newer"; build.bat, setup.bat) names Windows only, and Nebula reaches DLSS through it (streamline_bridge.h, vk/streamline_vk.h; host_window_win32.cpp is the only place that reports it supported). NVIDIA's DLSS SDK (github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS, commit "DLSS 310.9.16 SDK" of 2026-10-16) has lib/Linux_x86_64 with libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.310.9.16, libnvidia-ngx-dlssd.so and libnvidia-ngx-dlssg.so, libnvsdk_ngx.a and the Vulkan headers nvsdk_ngx_vk.h and nvsdk_ngx_helpers_vk.h: DLSS on Linux is NGX called directly, not Streamline. What a design needs: an NGX path in the Vulkan renderer for Linux (device and instance extensions NGX asks for, the NGX library next to the program, parameters and feature creation without Streamline), a Linux branch of the download prompt (vendor_download.cpp has only Windows files; the SDL host's upscaler_caps and its vendor_* functions return nothing) and the licence terms for shipping or fetching the library. Not read: the DLSS programming guide's list of driver versions and extensions for Linux (a PDF), and whether DLSS frame generation and Reflex have Linux paths. Not tried: any run of NGX on Linux. After the beta.
